subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.

spec.name: Warhound MX-77 Militarized Truck
spec.description: A low-poly cyberpunk 2077 armored 6x6 military truck with angular plated hull, neon underglow, roof turret, sensor mast and a cargo bed with missile pods.
spec.layout: Long, wide, angular armored 6x6 truck facing +Z. Front to back: a sloped armored bumper with a plow blade and light bar (z 3.7), a short wedge hood (z 2.2..3.5) with vents and glowing grille, a tall faceted two-door cab (z 0.5..2.3) with narrow cyan-tinted slit windshield and roof turret ring, then a long cargo bed (z -3.6..0.3) carrying a rocket pod rack, ammo crates and a rear sensor mast. Three axles: front at z=2.5, mid at z=-1.1, rear at z=-2.9 with big chunky 6-sided-ish low-poly wheels (radius 0.62) with glowing hub rims. Fender flares wrap each wheel. Chassis sits at y 0.55..1.35, cab top at y 2.55, turret and antennas to y 3.0. Style: dark gunmetal plates with panelled rivet paint, hazard yellow trim stripes, magenta and cyan neon strips along skirts, headlights, and underglow; decals/SVG for unit insignia, warning labels, kanji/number markings, screens. Every part uses the shared palette and keeps faceted blocky shapes with dense greeble detail.

parts.builds: Ladder-frame chassis and lower hull: two long side rails, cross members, panelled skirt armor along both sides with hazard-yellow chevron trim and neon magenta/cyan strips, belly plate with glowing underglow strips, exhaust stacks behind the cab, fuel tanks, fender flares over all six wheel arches (faceted wedges), mud flaps, tow hooks, rear bumper with taillight bars (warnRed glow), and rear tow hitch. Uses panelled(metal iron) paint, hazard stripe SVG decals, unit number markings on skirts. Does not include wheels, cab, hood or bed contents.
parts.attaches: Top at chassisTop supports cab (cabFloor), bed (bedFloor); wheel arches centred on axleFront/axleMid/axleRear; front end meets hood section at z=3.0.

parts.builds: Six chunky low-poly wheels (rubber tyres with lug tread blocks, 10-sided, radius 0.62, width 0.48), steel rims with bolt rings and glowing neonCyan inner hub rings, brake discs and calipers, axle housings with differential pumpkins, leaf spring packs, shock absorbers with coil springs (coil helper), steering links on the front axle, and a spare wheel is NOT included. Each wheel and its hub parts ride its wheel joint; axles and springs ride body. Wheels bottom at y=0.
parts.attaches: Wheel centres exactly at axleFront, axleMid, axleRear with x=±1.15; axle housings connect under chassis rails below chassisTop.

parts.builds: Armored crew cab and front end: faceted wedge hood with vents, glowing neonCyan grille slots and a hood-mounted light bar, sloped armored bumper with plow blade, hazard stripes, four headlights (white glow) plus magenta running strips, winch drum with cable, cab body with sloped angular armor plates, narrow slit glass windshield (glass colour with SVG reflection streaks and HUD glints), side windows with armored shutters, two hinged doors (doorL/doorR) with handles, number decals and unit insignia SVG, side mirrors with tiny screens, roof rack with antennas, roof air intake, cab-mounted searchlights, step rails, grab handles, interior seats and dashboard screens visible through glass (simple boxes with glowing SVG displays).
parts.attaches: Cab floor at cabFloor/chassisTop; roof at cabRoof where turretRing sits; rear wall at z=0.5 meets the bed; hood front at hoodFront and bumper at bumperFront.

parts.builds: Roof-mounted remote weapon station on turretRing: lathe base ring with yaw collar (turretYaw), faceted armored turret housing with sloped plates, twin heavy autocannon barrels with muzzle brakes and heat-sink fins, ammo box with belt feed, elevation cradle on turretGun joint, sensor ball camera with glowing cyan lens, smoke grenade launcher tubes (two banks of four), IFF panel with SVG markings, warning triangle decals, small antenna and glowing red status LEDs. Barrels point +Z.
parts.attaches: Base ring sits on turretRing at cabRoof height y=2.55-2.6; yaw joint at turretRing; gun cradle on turretGun.

parts.builds: Military cargo bed behind the cab: floor deck from bedFloor, angled armored side walls with panelled rivets and hazard trim, folded-down tailgate with latch details, a rocket pod rack (two 3x3 missile pods with olive/white tips and warnRed warning bands) on a hydraulic launcher frame, stacked ammo crates with SVG stencil labels, a roll of cable and jerrycans strapped with belts, a rear sensor mast at mastBase with dish antenna, blinking beacon and glowing neonMagenta lights, a big radar dish on a pole, tarp-covered cargo with olive camo paint, tie-down rings, floodlights and a rear rack with spare wheel. Everything stays within the bed footprint.
parts.attaches: Floor rests on bedFloor / chassisTop at y=1.35; front wall touches cab rear at z=0.5; mast at mastBase; rear edge at z=-3.7 flush with chassis end.

calls.reasoning:
I'm planning out a single compact function, using the provided Ctx type and helper utilities like box sizing without needing extra imports.

For the vehicle geometry, I'm working through side-profile extrusions for the cab and hood, calculating coordinate points for the windshield slope, roof line, and hood mount to get the proportions right within the box dimensions.

Still placing windshield geometry... now I'm adding side window planes with textures, armored shutter bars on top, and door panel boxes positioned at the door joints.

Adding the plow blade as a sloped steel wedge across the front, plus hazard stripe texture on a bumper-front plane, and positioning glowing headlight boxes up on the bumper near the hood line.

Now I'm laying out the grille details on the hood's front face: cyan glowing slots spaced across the center, paired headlight boxes at varying sizes flanking them, all set at the hood's forward z-position with thin depth.

Then I'm positioning a magenta glow strip along the bumper plane above the hazard lights, and working out the hood vent placement by computing the slope angle of the hood's top surface so the vent boxes can be tilted to match, rotating them about the x-axis to align with the sloped geometry.

Vent slats get placed in rows along the slope with alternating positions, then I add a light bar on the hood with six alternating cyan and magenta emitter segments, and start positioning a winch drum near the front bumper, adjusting its location since it initially overlaps the bumper box.

I resolve the overlap by splitting the blade to a lower y-range and the bumper to an upper y-range with ribs, placing the winch drum between them at y 0.87, z 3.58, radius 0.1.

Simplifying the bumper and blade profiles with separate extrusions, adding a small winch cylinder with a cable rod extending to a hook. Then I'm sketching the roof rack with posts and rails, plus a turret ring mounted on the roof box.

I'm placing the roof-mounted details now: a turret centered at z 0.9, a rack spanning z 1.5-1.8, searchlights at x ±0.9, rear corner antennas, and an air intake box at x -0.85 with louvres carved in.

Now working through mirror placement, trying to find a spot that doesn't collide with the door or windshield geometry—considering mounting the arm and mirror head near the forward cab corner instead of directly on the door.

Adding grab handles and A-pillar rods near the door. For the interior I'm realizing the solid cab extrude will occlude any seats or dash placed inside, so I need a workaround -- maybe treating windows as textured cutouts rather than true transparency since cutting the hull open is too complex for this build.

Instead I'll fake occupied interiors by drawing seat silhouettes, headrests, glowing screens, and a driver shape directly in the SVG texture so they read as visible through the glass without needing real transparency, keeping windshield glow subtle (~0.4) so lighting stays believable. For the cab exterior I'm planning angular armor plates: rotated wedge boxes on the sides, slanted roof-edge plates, and A-pillar plates, plus starting on the rear structure.

Now I'm working on rear details (bed junction, roof overhang plate, rear window slit, back armor plate with hazard lights), choosing panelled textures with moderate rivet density for the hull and plates, and sketching out door decals — a "77" number, a hexagonal hound-head insignia, and a warning label — figuring out how the texture orientation maps onto the door's outward-facing plane.

Working through the viewing geometry so the decal text reads correctly on each side: for a viewer standing at +x looking toward -x, the right-hand direction comes out as -z, meaning the truck's front sits to the viewer's left, which checks out as the natural reading direction for a side panel; the mirrored case on the -x side should automatically read correctly too, so I'm trusting the auto-orientation from the aim direction while leaving roll unconstrained for now.

Now I'm sketching the cab door details: positioning a door panel roughly 0.9 by 0.4 at the lower section, figuring out box dimensions spanning y from about 1.45 to 2.45 and z from 0.85 to 1.95, placing a window plane near the top of the door, a shutter bar above it, a number decal around mid-height, and an insignia circle nearby, plus locating the door hinge point.

I'm consolidating all the door markings — number, insignia, and label — into a single combined texture plane so it can be reused by mirroring for the opposite door, then adding a small handle box offset from the door's outer edge.

Now I'm planning the hazard stripe planes along the hood sides, and sketching out the SVG textures needed: hazard chevrons, a windshield with gradient glass and interior silhouettes, a side window, and the door texture with number, insignia, and "WARHOUND" label.

I'm sketching helper functions for building parts—box and cylinder creators keyed to bone attachments and rotations, plus a glow helper for emissive parts—while keeping a tight color palette with just a few custom additions beyond the base set.

I'm defining the cab outline shape as a series of coordinate points to extrude into the body, centering the extrusion thickness on the drawing plane and relying on panel-reading paint logic for surface shading.

Now I'm positioning the cab behind the hood with proper x-range and y-height matching the chassis top, then adding angled wedge boxes for roof chamfers rotated outward on each side.

Working out the rotation signs so the roof edges slant down correctly on the +x and -x sides, then adding cab shoulder plates and starting the windshield frame geometry.

Now I'm computing the slope angle for the visor box above the windshield slit and figuring out the rotation needed to align a thin box flush against that sloped plane.

Computing positions for the windshield plane and its frame pillars, aligning them to the slope direction with the correct offset and size so the glass sits centered within the frame. Now moving on to position the searchlights.

Placing paired searchlight cylinders on the front roof, keeping them slightly under the max height limit even though antennas can extend higher. I'm also setting up a helper for z-axis cylinders via rotation, and sketching out a sweep for the cable running from the drum to the hook.

Now I'm adding bumper hazard stripes and a magenta underglow strip beneath the bumper, then working on hood details—a raised center ridge, vent slats positioned along the sloped hood surface, and tuning the rotation angle so everything slants correctly toward the front.

I'm positioning the headlight housings and lenses as dark/glowing boxes on each side, checking that the grille slots and lamp placements stay within the hood's width without overlapping past the edges.

Still working out the bumper geometry...

I'm positioning the winch drum as a small cylinder between the blade and bumper, adding flange caps at its ends, then setting up a loop to place both doors symmetrically and considering a rear armor plate near the hull's back wall.

Now I'm adding a rear roof lip plate extending across the top, skipping the exhaust since it's not part of this build, and sketching a hazard stripe trim along the lower cab sides beneath the doors.

Adding door trim and grab handles...

Now I'm planning roof antennas with tapered spikes and glowing warning-red tips at the rear corners, plus a roof rack with rails and a turret ring structure.

Rack rods run along z at x ±1.05 with corner posts, crossbars, and slats, keeping clear of the central turret area. I'm placing small cargo boxes and searchlights on the rack, and figuring out where to fit the air intake and antennas without colliding with the turret or rack geometry.

Positioning the intake near the turret front as a low faceted wedge with louvre slats, centered at x=0, keeping its height thin so it clears the turret ring and barrel housing.

For the side details, I'm adding frame boxes around the window to form an armored shutter effect—top bar, bottom bar, and two side bars with thin thickness and depth—plus a small hood-mounted light bar near the windshield.

I'm mirroring the door frame symmetrically on the opposite side, then moving on to writing the hazard-stripe texture as an SVG with alternating yellow and black diagonal polygons.

For the windshield texture, I'm laying out a cyan-to-dark gradient background, a dashboard strip with glowing cyan and magenta screen panels, seat headrests with a driver silhouette, motion streak polygons, and a small HUD crosshair with text. I'm then sketching a similar glass-and-silhouette treatment for the side window before starting on the door texture.

Now I'm designing the door panel over a transparent background: a hexagonal insignia with a simplified hound-head emblem, bold "MX-77" lettering, and a tiny red "WARNING" label strip, keeping text legible against whatever paint color shows through. I'm also planning a small mirror screen texture with dark cyan arrow lines, and working out where to attach the mirror geometry relative to the door hinge bone so the stalk and mirror body sit correctly in 3D space.

I'm placing the mirror head and stalk at precise coordinates on the cab's front shoulder plate, and setting up the screen plane orientation so it faces outward correctly. I'm confirming the rotation parameter naming convention and how the glow effect clones materials for boxes, then adding a dark backing box behind the cyan grille.

Now I'm working out the grille slot spacing—seven glowing slots spaced evenly to fit within the backing width, checking that they align properly with the headlight positions on either side. I'm also planning the hood's side strip, chevrons, and roof ridge details, then turning to the cab's front shoulder area between the hood and windshield, where I'll add angled armor plates and amber marker lights above the cab front wall.

Adding armor plates to cab sides...

Writing helper functions for box and cylinder geometry...
